recipes.title: Matbucha
recipes.description: Tomatoes and roasted peppers cooked down slowly into a sweet, gently spicy spread. The dish that opens every Moroccan table.
instructions: Char the peppers over an open flame until blackened. Seal in a bag for 10 minutes, then peel and cut into strips.
Score the tomatoes, blanch 30 seconds in boiling water, peel and chop roughly.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan, add the garlic and fry for 30 seconds only — do not let it brown.
Add tomatoes, peppers, paprika, cumin and chili. Cook uncovered over low heat for 45–60 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Once the liquid has evaporated and the mixture is thick and glossy, season with salt and sugar. Serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Zaalouk — Eggplant Salad
recipes.description: Eggplant and tomato mashed together with garlic, cumin and coriander into a rich, smoky spread. Perhaps the best-loved salad in Morocco.
instructions: Roast the eggplants at 220°C for about 35 minutes until completely soft and collapsed. Cool, peel and mash.
Peel and chop the tomatoes. Cook in a pan with olive oil and garlic for about 15 minutes until softened.
Add the mashed eggplant flesh, paprika and cumin. Continue cooking 15 minutes, mashing with a wooden spoon.
When the mixture is thick and no liquid remains, turn off the heat and stir in coriander, parsley and lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve warm or at room temperature with fresh bread.

recipes.title: Taktouka — Roasted Pepper Salad
recipes.description: Charred green peppers and tomatoes in olive oil and garlic. Simple, sweet and smoky — served at almost every meal.
instructions: Char the peppers on a grill or flame until the skin blackens. Wrap in plastic for 10 minutes, peel, deseed and tear into strips.
Peel the tomatoes (a brief blanch makes this easy) and chop roughly.
Heat the olive oil with the crushed garlic, add the tomatoes and cook 15 minutes until they break down.
Add the pepper strips, paprika and cumin. Cook another 10–15 minutes until the liquid reduces.
Season with salt, scatter over the parsley and serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Moroccan Carrot Salad
recipes.description: Cooked carrots in a lemon, garlic and cumin dressing, with a touch of cinnamon to draw out the sweetness. Orange, glossy and addictive.
instructions: Peel the carrots and slice into rounds about half a centimetre thick.
Boil in salted water for 10–12 minutes — tender but still holding their shape. Drain.
Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika and cinnamon in a bowl.
Toss the hot carrots in the dressing — warm they absorb far more. Season with salt.
Chill at least an hour, and stir in the coriander just before serving.

recipes.title: Beetroot Salad with Cumin
recipes.description: Sweet beetroot with cumin, lemon and olive oil. A deep red that balances everything else on the table.
instructions: Wash the beetroots without peeling and boil for 40–45 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Cool slightly, peel by hand (the skin slips off) and cut into cubes.
Whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, garlic and sugar.
Toss the beetroot in the dressing and season with salt.
Chill for at least half an hour and scatter parsley over before serving.

recipes.title: Preserved Lemons
recipes.description: Lemons and nothing but salt, cured for a month into a deep salty flavour with no substitute. The ingredient that makes a tagine a tagine.
instructions: Wash and dry the lemons well. Cut each one lengthwise into quarters — but not all the way through, so the base stays joined.
Open each lemon and pack the inside generously with coarse salt.
Press the lemons into a sterilised jar, layer on layer, scattering salt between the layers.
Add the bay leaves and peppercorns and pour in lemon juice until the lemons are fully covered. Seal tightly.
Leave at room temperature for 3–4 weeks, turning the jar every couple of days. To use: rinse, discard the pulp and use only the peel.

recipes.title: Moroccan Harissa
recipes.description: Chili paste with garlic, cumin and caraway. Hot, deep and faintly smoky — one spoonful changes any dish.
instructions: Soak the dried chilies in hot water for 30 minutes until softened. Drain and remove stems and seeds.
Toast the cumin, coriander and caraway seeds in a dry pan for a minute or two until fragrant. Grind in a mortar.
Blitz the chilies, garlic, toasted spices and salt in a food processor to a coarse paste.
Add the olive oil gradually while blending until smooth and glossy, then stir in the lemon juice.
Transfer to a jar, cover with a layer of olive oil and keep refrigerated for up to a month.

recipes.title: Eggplant in Chermoula
recipes.description: Fried eggplant slices soaking up chermoula — the coriander, garlic and cumin sauce that runs through the whole Moroccan kitchen.
instructions: Cut the eggplants into 1cm slices, salt them and leave 30 minutes. Pat thoroughly dry — this is what stops them drinking oil.
Fry the slices in deep oil until golden on both sides. Transfer to paper towels.
For the chermoula: finely chop coriander, parsley and garlic, then mix with cumin, paprika, lemon juice and olive oil.
Layer the eggplant slices on a serving plate, spreading chermoula between the layers.
Cover and chill at least two hours — the flavour improves markedly. Serve cold or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Orange and Olive Salad
recipes.description: Orange slices with black olives, red onion and cinnamon. A sweet-salty contrast that clears the palate after something heavy.
instructions: Peel the oranges down to the flesh — removing all the white pith — and slice into rounds.
Slice the red onion very thinly and soak in cold water for 10 minutes to soften its bite. Drain.
Arrange the orange slices on a flat plate and scatter the onion and olives over them.
Drizzle with olive oil and orange blossom water, then dust with cinnamon and a pinch of salt.
Chill 20 minutes, garnish with torn mint leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Marinated Olives
recipes.description: Green olives in olive oil, preserved lemon, garlic and coriander. They sit on the table from the first moment and disappear first.
instructions: Rinse the olives well in cold water and dry. If very salty, soak in water for an hour, changing the water twice.
Rinse the preserved lemon, discard the pulp and cut the peel into thin strips.
Combine the olives, preserved lemon, garlic, coriander, paprika and cumin in a bowl.
Pour over the olive oil and lemon juice and toss until every olive is coated.
Transfer to a jar and leave refrigerated at least 24 hours before serving. Keeps two weeks.

recipes.title: Harira
recipes.description: The lentil, chickpea and beef soup that breaks the fast in Morocco. Thick, tart with tomato and heavy with fresh herbs.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and sear the beef cubes on all sides until browned.
Add onion, celery, turmeric and ginger and fry 5 minutes. Add the soaked chickpeas and 2 litres of water.
Bring to the boil, lower the heat and simmer covered for an hour until chickpeas and meat are tender.
Add the grated tomatoes, lentils and half the herbs. Cook a further 25 minutes.
Whisk the flour into a cup of cold water until lump-free and pour into the pot in a thin stream, stirring constantly — this is what gives harira its body.
Cook another 10 minutes, season with salt and pepper and stir in the remaining coriander and parsley before serving.

recipes.title: Bissara — Fava Bean Soup
recipes.description: A velvet-smooth dried fava soup with garlic, cumin and olive oil. Winter breakfast in every Moroccan market.
instructions: Soak the fava beans in cold water overnight. Drain and rinse well.
Cook the beans with the garlic in 1.5 litres of water for about an hour, until they collapse completely.
Blend with a stick blender until entirely smooth. If too thick, add boiling water gradually.
Return to the heat, add cumin, paprika, salt and pepper and cook a further 5 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls with a generous drizzle of olive oil, lemon juice and an extra pinch of cumin on top.

recipes.title: Vegetable Chorba
recipes.description: A root vegetable soup with saffron and coriander, finished with fine noodles. Light, fragrant and comforting.
instructions: Fry the onion in olive oil in a large pot until translucent.
Add turmeric and saffron and stir for 30 seconds — the heat releases the colour and aroma.
Add all the root vegetables, the tomatoes and 1.5 litres of water. Bring to the boil and cook 30 minutes.
Add the courgettes and noodles and cook a further 8 minutes until the noodles are soft.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the fresh coriander and serve at once.

recipes.title: Parve Lentil Harira
recipes.description: Harira without the meat — lentils, chickpeas and tomato, with the same herbs and the same body. Fully parve.
instructions: Fry the onion and celery in olive oil until soft, add turmeric, ginger and cinnamon and stir for a minute.
Add the grated tomatoes and cook 10 minutes until reduced.
Add the lentils, chickpeas and 1.5 litres of water. Cook 30 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Whisk the flour into half a cup of cold water and pour in, stirring constantly. Cook 10 minutes until thickened.
Season and stir in plenty of chopped coriander. Serve with a wedge of lemon.

recipes.title: Chickpea and Cumin Soup
recipes.description: Chickpeas simmered until they melt, with plenty of cumin and garlic. One soup that warms a whole evening.
instructions: Drain the soaked chickpeas and cook in 2 litres of water with the bay leaf for about an hour, until completely tender.
Meanwhile fry the onion and garlic in olive oil until lightly golden.
Add the cumin and paprika to the pan and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Tip the onion mixture into the chickpea pot and cook together a further 15 minutes.
Blend about a third of the soup and return it to the pot — this gives body while leaving whole chickpeas. Season and finish with lemon and parsley.

recipes.title: Pumpkin and Saffron Soup
recipes.description: Sweet pumpkin with saffron, ginger and a pinch of cinnamon. Deep orange, velvety — and not a drop of cream.
instructions: Steep the saffron threads in 2 tablespoons of hot water and set aside — this draws out their full colour.
Fry the onion and carrot in olive oil for 7 minutes until softened.
Add the pumpkin cubes, ginger, cinnamon and 1.2 litres of water. Cook 25 minutes until the pumpkin collapses.
Blend until completely smooth and stir in the saffron water. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with toasted flaked almonds on top and a drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.title: Tomato and Vermicelli Soup
recipes.description: A plain tomato soup with fine noodles and coriander. The one you make when there is no time — and finish to the last spoon.
instructions: Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent, without browning.
Add the tomato paste and paprika and stir for a minute to bring out the sweetness.
Add the grated tomatoes, sugar and 1 litre of water. Cook 20 minutes over medium heat.
Add the broken noodles and cook 6–8 minutes until soft.
Season with salt and pepper and scatter over plenty of fresh coriander.

recipes.title: Loubia — White Beans
recipes.description: White beans in a tomato, paprika and cumin sauce, cooked until creamy. A whole meal with nothing but bread.
instructions: Drain the beans and cook in 1.5 litres of water for 45 minutes, until almost tender. Do not salt at this stage.
Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil, add the paste, paprika and cumin and stir for a minute.
Add the grated tomatoes and cook 10 minutes until the sauce reduces.
Pour the sauce into the bean pot and cook together a further 30 minutes over low heat.
Season with salt and pepper only now — salting early keeps beans tough — and stir in the coriander.

recipes.title: Chicken Harira
recipes.description: A lighter harira built on chicken instead of beef. The same depth in less cooking time.
instructions: Sear the chicken legs in olive oil in a large pot until golden on both sides, then set aside.
In the same pot fry the onion and celery, add turmeric and ginger and stir.
Return the chicken, add 1.8 litres of water and cook 35 minutes. Lift out the chicken, pull the meat from the bone and return the meat.
Add the tomatoes, lentils and chickpeas and cook 20 minutes.
Thicken with the flour whisked into cold water, stirring as you pour; cook 10 minutes, season and finish with fresh herbs.

recipes.title: Hsoua — Barley Soup
recipes.description: A rustic barley soup from the Atlas mountains, with cumin and olive oil. Few ingredients, a great deal of flavour.
instructions: Rinse the barley in cold water until the water runs clear.
Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft, add turmeric and cumin and stir.
Add the grated tomato, the barley and 1.5 litres of water. Bring to the boil.
Lower the heat and cook 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the barley is tender and the soup thick.
Season, stir in the coriander and finish with a generous drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
recipes.description: Morocco's best-known tagine. Chicken cooked slowly in a saffron and ginger sauce, with preserved lemon and green olives.
instructions: Make the marinade: combine olive oil, garlic, saffron steeped in a little hot water, ginger, turmeric, half the herbs, salt and pepper.
Rub the chicken pieces with the marinade and refrigerate at least an hour — overnight is better.
Lay the sliced onion in the base of a tagine or heavy pot and set the chicken and all its marinade on top.
Add half a cup of water, cover and cook over low heat for 50 minutes. Do not stir — let the steam do the work.
Rinse the preserved lemons, discard the pulp and cut the peel into strips. Add with the olives and cook a further 20 minutes.
Uncover and cook a final 5 minutes to reduce the sauce. Finish with lemon juice and the remaining herbs. Olive oil stands in for smen here, which keeps the dish entirely meat.

recipes.title: Lamb Tagine with Prunes and Almonds
recipes.description: Lamb falling apart in a cinnamon and honey sauce, with dried prunes and toasted almonds. The festival dish of Morocco.
instructions: Sear the lamb cubes in olive oil in a heavy pot until deeply browned on all sides. This is the foundation of the whole flavour.
Add the onion, ginger, ground cinnamon, saffron and cinnamon sticks. Fry 5 minutes.
Add water to cover the meat, bring to the boil, lower the heat and cook covered for two hours until the lamb falls apart.
Meanwhile soak the prunes in hot water for 20 minutes. Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Lift out the meat, reduce the sauce by half, add the honey and prunes and cook 15 minutes until thick and glossy.
Return the meat to warm through, scatter over the almonds and sesame and serve. Olive oil replaces the traditional butter here — the dish is meat.

recipes.title: Kefta Tagine with Eggs
recipes.description: Spiced meatballs in a hot tomato sauce, with eggs cracked in at the end. Eaten straight from the dish with bread.
instructions: Mix the ground beef with grated onion, parsley, a teaspoon of cumin, half a tablespoon of paprika, salt and pepper. Knead well.
Roll into walnut-sized balls and chill 20 minutes so they hold together.
Make the sauce: fry the garlic in olive oil, add the grated tomatoes, harissa and the remaining cumin and paprika. Cook 15 minutes.
Set the meatballs into the simmering sauce, cover and cook 20 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally.
Crack the eggs between the meatballs, cover and cook 5–7 minutes until the whites set and the yolks are still soft.
Scatter over coriander and serve hot from the dish. There is no dairy here — eggs are parve, so the dish stays meat.

recipes.title: Beef Tagine with Quince
recipes.description: Beef in a saffron sauce with caramelised quince. The fruit's sharpness cuts the richness exactly right.
instructions: Sear the beef cubes in olive oil until browned all over, then set aside.
Fry the onion in the same pot until soft, then add the saffron, ginger and cinnamon stick.
Return the meat, cover with water and cook over low heat for two hours until fully tender.
Meanwhile halve the quinces, core them and cut into thick wedges. Hold in lemon water so they do not darken.
Fry the quince wedges in a pan with the sugar and honey until golden and caramelised on both sides.
Lay the quince over the meat, cook together for a final 15 minutes and season. Serve with bread or couscous.

recipes.title: Dafina — Moroccan Shabbat Stew
recipes.description: The Shabbat pot of Moroccan Jews. Beef, chickpeas, potatoes, wheat and eggs cooked overnight until everything turns brown and sweet.
instructions: Sear the meat in olive oil at the bottom of a large heavy pot until well browned.
Arrange the soaked chickpeas, wheat berries, onions and garlic around the meat.
Lay the whole potatoes, dates and the eggs in their shells on top — the eggs take their brown colour from the long cooking.
Mix the spices with 2 cups of water and pour in. Add water until everything is just covered.
Bring to the boil, reduce to the lowest heat and cover tightly. Move to a 100°C oven or leave on a hotplate overnight — 10 to 12 hours.
Serve hot: the meat, the browned eggs, the potatoes and the wheat, each separately on the plate. No dairy at any stage.

recipes.title: Mrouzia — Lamb with Honey and Raisins
recipes.description: A sweet, heavily spiced lamb stew with ras el hanout, honey and raisins. One of the oldest dishes in the Moroccan kitchen.
instructions: Rub the lamb pieces with ras el hanout, cinnamon, saffron and salt and leave an hour in the fridge.
Sear the meat in olive oil in a heavy pot until browned, add the onion and fry 10 minutes.
Add water to cover and cook covered over low heat for two and a half hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Soak the raisins in hot water 15 minutes and drain. Toast the almonds until golden.
Lift out the meat, reduce the sauce, add the honey and raisins and cook 20 minutes to a thick syrup.
Return the meat, scatter over almonds and sesame and serve. Olive oil in place of smen keeps the dish meat.

recipes.title: Fish Tagine in Chermoula
recipes.description: White fish fillets on a bed of vegetables, wrapped in chermoula. Fin-and-scale fish only — the dish is parve.

ingredients.name: sea bream or sea bass fillets

instructions: Make the chermoula: blend coriander, garlic, cumin, paprika, lemon juice and olive oil to a green paste.
Spread half the chermoula over the fish fillets and chill 30 minutes.
Lay a layer of potato and carrot in the base of the tagine, season, and top with the red pepper.
Set the fish on the vegetables, arrange the tomato slices and olives over it and pour on the remaining chermoula.
Carefully add half a cup of water at the side of the dish, cover and cook over low heat for 40 minutes.
Check the potatoes are tender and serve straight from the dish. Fin-and-scale fish only — no shellfish here.

recipes.title: Chreime — Fish in Hot Sauce
recipes.description: Fish steaks in a paprika, garlic and cumin sauce with real heat. A holiday dish of North African Jews, eaten with challah dipped in the sauce.
instructions: Salt the fish steaks and leave 20 minutes. Rinse and dry thoroughly.
Heat the oil in a wide pan, add the garlic and fry 30 seconds — do not brown it.
Add both paprikas, the cumin and the tomato paste and immediately stir in half a cup of water so the spices do not burn.
Add another cup of water and the chilies, bring to the boil and cook the sauce 10 minutes.
Lay the fish steaks in the sauce in a single layer, cover and cook 15 minutes — turning once, carefully.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander. Serve warm with bread. The fish is parve, so it can go beside a meat or a dairy course.

recipes.title: Mechoui — Slow-Roast Lamb Shoulder
recipes.description: Lamb shoulder roasted for hours until it melts, with nothing but cumin and salt. Complete simplicity.
instructions: Mix the olive oil, garlic, ground cumin, paprika, turmeric, salt and pepper into a paste.
Score the shoulder in several places and rub the paste in well, right into the cuts.
Refrigerate at least two hours — overnight is better.
Set in a deep tray with a cup of water, cover tightly with foil and roast at 160°C for about two and a half hours.
Remove the foil, raise to 200°C and roast a further 30–40 minutes until the outside is golden and crisp.
Serve with a small bowl of coarse salt and cumin seeds — each person dips their own. That is the Moroccan way.

recipes.title: Chicken Tagine with Root Vegetables
recipes.description: Chicken with carrot, potato and turnip in a pale saffron sauce. A weekday tagine — plain and filling.
instructions: Rub the chicken pieces with turmeric, ginger, saffron, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Lay sliced onion in the base of the pot and set the spiced chicken on top.
Add a cup of water, cover and cook 25 minutes over medium-low heat.
Arrange the carrot, potato and turnip around the chicken. Cook covered a further 30 minutes.
Add the courgettes — they cook fast — and give it a final 12 minutes.
Scatter over fresh herbs and serve straight from the dish, with the sauce.

recipes.title: Seven Vegetable Couscous
recipes.description: The classic Friday couscous: semolina steamed three times, a rich vegetable broth and meat that falls apart. A dish for a whole family.
instructions: Sear the meat in olive oil in the base of the couscoussier, add onion, tomatoes, turmeric, ginger and saffron and fry 10 minutes.
Add 3 litres of water and a tied bundle of herbs, bring to the boil and cook 45 minutes.
First steaming: spread the couscous in a bowl, sprinkle with water and olive oil and rub through with your hands. Move to the top section and steam 20 minutes uncovered.
Return the couscous to the bowl, break it up with a fork, sprinkle more water and steam again 20 minutes. Repeat a third time — this is what gives separate, airy grains.
Add carrot, turnip and cabbage to the broth and cook 20 minutes. Add pumpkin, courgettes and chickpeas and cook a further 15 minutes.
To serve: a mound of couscous in a bowl, the meat and vegetables on top and a ladle of broth alongside. Olive oil instead of butter — the dish is meat.

recipes.title: Couscous Tfaya
recipes.description: Couscous with caramelised onion, raisins and cinnamon over chicken. Sweet, golden and special — an occasion couscous.
instructions: Cook the chicken with one onion, saffron, ginger, olive oil, salt and pepper in 1.5 litres of water for about 45 minutes.
For the tfaya: fry the remaining 4 onions in olive oil over low heat for 40 minutes, until brown and sweet.
Add soaked raisins, honey and cinnamon to the onions and cook together 15 minutes to a thick, glossy mixture.
Steam the couscous three times, 20 minutes each, breaking it up and sprinkling with broth in between.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Spread the couscous on a large platter, the chicken over it, the tfaya on top and scatter the almonds. Serve with a bowl of broth.

recipes.title: Parve Vegetable Couscous
recipes.description: All the flavour of Moroccan couscous with no meat at all. A well-spiced vegetable broth you can serve beside anything.
instructions: Fry the onion in olive oil until golden, add the grated tomatoes and all the spices and cook 10 minutes.
Add 2 litres of water and the bundle of herbs and bring to the boil.
Steam the couscous a first time for 20 minutes, break it up, sprinkle with water and olive oil and steam again.
Add carrot and turnip to the broth and cook 20 minutes. Add pumpkin, courgettes and chickpeas and cook 15 minutes.
Steam the couscous a third time — a final 15 minutes.
Serve the couscous with the vegetables on top and broth alongside. Fully parve — it works next to a dairy course too.

recipes.title: Chicken Pastilla
recipes.description: A crisp layered pie filled with spiced chicken, egg and sweet almonds, dusted with sugar and cinnamon. Sweet and savoury at once — the dish Morocco serves to honour a guest.
instructions: Cook the chicken with onion, saffron, ginger, olive oil, salt, pepper and a little water for 50 minutes. Lift out, bone and tear into pieces.
Reduce the cooking liquid to a thick sauce, lower the heat and pour in the beaten eggs, stirring until thick and curd-like. Stir in the parsley.
Fry the almonds in oil until golden, drain and grind coarsely with the icing sugar and a teaspoon of cinnamon.
Oil a round tin and line it with the pastry sheets in layers, brushing each with olive oil and letting the edges hang over the side.
Fill in layers: the egg mixture, the shredded chicken, then the sweet almonds. Fold the overhanging edges in and cover with 2–3 more sheets.
Bake at 190°C for about 35 minutes until golden. Dust with icing sugar and lines of cinnamon and serve hot. Olive oil in place of butter — the dish is meat.

recipes.title: Meat Briouats
recipes.description: Crisp pastry triangles filled with spiced ground meat. Fried golden and gone from the plate within minutes.
instructions: Fry the onion in olive oil until soft, add the ground beef and fry until browned and crumbly.
Add cumin, paprika, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook 5 minutes until all the liquid has gone. Cool.
Stir in the parsley and the beaten egg — the egg is what holds the filling together.
Cut the pastry into strips 8cm wide. Place a spoon of filling at one end and fold in alternating triangles to the end of the strip.
Seal the end with a little water and press. Repeat until the filling is used up.
Fry in deep oil over medium heat until golden on both sides, about 3 minutes. Drain on paper and serve hot.

recipes.title: Spinach Briouats
recipes.description: The parve version — spinach, coriander and preserved lemon in crisp pastry. Lighter, and no less good.
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for a minute, drain and refresh in cold water. Squeeze out hard — this is critical so the pastry does not go soggy.
Chop the squeezed spinach roughly.
Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil, add the spinach, cumin, salt and pepper and cook 5 minutes until dry.
Stir in the chopped preserved lemon and coriander and cool completely.
Cut the pastry into strips, fill and fold into triangles. Seal with a little water.
Fry in deep oil until golden, or bake at 200°C for about 20 minutes. Parve — it suits any table.

recipes.title: Msemen — Layered Flatbread
recipes.description: A square bread that lies on the pan and opens into dozens of paper-thin layers. The secret is the stretching and folding, not the dough.
instructions: Mix flour, semolina, yeast, sugar and salt. Add the water gradually and knead 10 minutes to a very soft, elastic dough.
Divide into egg-sized balls, oil each one and leave to rest 20 minutes, covered.
Flatten a ball on an oiled surface and stretch it by hand until almost transparent — working from the centre outwards.
Drizzle with oil and dust semolina over the whole surface. Fold the sides in to make a strip, then again into a square.
Rest 10 minutes, then gently flatten into a square about half a centimetre thick.
Cook in a dry hot pan for 3–4 minutes a side until the layers turn golden. Serve hot with honey. Oil instead of butter — parve.

recipes.title: Harcha — Semolina Bread
recipes.description: Round semolina cakes cooked in a pan, crisp outside and soft within. A breakfast with butter and honey — the one dairy recipe here.
instructions: Mix semolina, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Add the soft butter and rub between your fingers until the mixture looks like damp sand.
Add the milk gradually and stir gently — only until the dough comes together. Do not knead.
Let the dough rest 15 minutes so the semolina absorbs the liquid.
Shape rounds about 1.5cm thick and coat both sides in dry semolina.
Cook in a dry pan over low heat 8–10 minutes a side until a golden crust forms. Serve hot. Note: this is a dairy recipe — do not serve at a meat meal.

recipes.title: Batbout — Moroccan Pita
recipes.description: A pocket bread baked in a pan rather than an oven, puffing into a perfect pocket. Soft, spongy and still fresh a day later.
instructions: Mix all the flours with the yeast, sugar and salt.
Add the warm water and olive oil and knead 10 minutes to a smooth, soft, non-sticky dough.
Cover and prove an hour in a warm place until doubled.
Divide into 10 balls, flatten each into a round about half a centimetre thick and set on a floured cloth.
Prove again for 30 minutes — this is what makes the pocket open.
Cook in a dry hot pan for 3 minutes a side. The bread will puff by itself. Move to a clean cloth to keep it soft.

recipes.title: Mofletta
recipes.description: The thin Mimouna pancake, stacked high and eaten with honey. The sign that Passover is over.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add the water gradually and knead 8 minutes to a very soft, almost pourable dough.
Cover and prove 30 minutes.
Oil your hands well, form small walnut-sized balls and set on an oiled tray. Oil the tops too.
Stretch a ball between oiled palms into the thinnest possible round — almost transparent.
Cook in a dry pan: lay a round down, and once the underside sets, place a fresh round on top and flip them together.
Carry on this way — each new mofletta cooks the previous one on its second side. One hot stack, with honey. The dough is entirely parve.

recipes.title: Chebakia
recipes.description: Fried rose-shaped cookies steeped in honey and coated in sesame. The sweet that comes with every bowl of harira, at Ramadan and every festival.
instructions: Mix the flour, ground sesame, almonds, saffron, anise, cinnamon and yeast in a large bowl.
Add the oil, vinegar, orange blossom water and water gradually. Knead 15 minutes to a firm, even dough. Rest an hour.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into rectangles. Score 4 slits along each rectangle.
Thread a finger through alternate slits and pinch the ends together — this forms the rose shape.
Fry in deep oil over medium heat until golden, about 5 minutes. Lift out and transfer straight into warm honey.
Steep in the honey 7–10 minutes until soaked through, lift out with a slotted spoon and scatter with sesame. Dry on a rack.

recipes.title: Ghriba — Almond Cookies
recipes.description: Almond cookies cracked across the top, soft within and buried in icing sugar. Three main ingredients and a perfect result.
instructions: Mix the ground almonds, icing sugar and baking powder in a bowl.
Beat the eggs with the orange blossom water, lemon zest and oil and add to the dry mixture.
Stir to a sticky, even dough. Chill 30 minutes — colder is easier to roll.
Form walnut-sized balls and roll each thickly in icing sugar.
Set on a lined tray with space between them and press each one lightly to flatten.
Bake at 170°C for 15–18 minutes — they will crack on top and stay soft inside. No butter here: parve.

recipes.title: Kaab el Ghazal — Gazelle Horns
recipes.description: Fine crescents filled with almond paste and orange blossom. So delicate the pastry is almost see-through.

ingredients.name: orange blossom water for the filling

instructions: For the filling: mix ground almonds, sugar, cinnamon, lemon zest and orange blossom water into a rollable paste.
Roll the paste into thin 6cm logs and bend each slightly into a crescent.
For the pastry: knead flour, oil, orange blossom water, salt and a little water for 10 minutes to a smooth, very elastic dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Roll the dough as thin as you can — almost transparent. Lay the crescents on it, spaced apart.
Fold the dough over the filling, press around each crescent and push the air out. Cut with a wheel and shape into a curved horn.
Prick each one with a toothpick and bake at 180°C for 15–18 minutes until only pale — they must not brown. Dust with icing sugar.

recipes.title: Sellou — Sfouf
recipes.description: Toasted flour, almonds, sesame and honey, eaten by the spoonful. Not a cake, not a cookie — entirely its own thing.
instructions: Toast the flour on a tray at 160°C for about 25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes — until light brown and smelling nutty.
Toast the almonds until golden, and the sesame in a dry pan until it starts to pop.
Grind two thirds of the almonds and most of the sesame coarsely in a processor. Keep some whole for decoration.
In a large bowl mix the toasted flour, ground nuts, icing sugar, cinnamon, anise and mastic.
Warm the oil and honey together and pour into the dry mixture, stirring, until it has the texture of wet sand that clumps in the hand.
Transfer to a serving bowl, press into a dome and decorate with whole almonds. Keeps for weeks in a sealed container.

recipes.title: Mhencha — Almond Coil
recipes.description: A long filled pastry tube wound into a spiral like a coiled snake. Remarkably impressive and easier than it looks.
instructions: Mix the ground almonds, sugar, cinnamon, orange zest and orange blossom water into a moist, rollable paste.
Overlap 2 filo sheets, brush with oil and lay a sausage of filling along one edge.
Roll into a long narrow tube. Repeat with the remaining sheets.
Coil one tube into a spiral at the centre of an oiled round tin, and join the next tubes on to continue the spiral.
Brush with beaten egg yolk and bake at 180°C for about 35 minutes until deeply golden.
Drizzle warm honey over the hot pastry and scatter flaked almonds and icing sugar. Oil instead of butter — parve, so it can follow a meat meal.

recipes.title: Moroccan Mint Tea
recipes.description: Green tea, fresh mint and plenty of sugar, poured from a height to raise the foam. Not a drink — a ritual.
instructions: Rinse the tea leaves with a cup of boiling water and pour it straight off — this removes the bitterness.
Add half a litre of boiling water to the pot and simmer over low heat for 3 minutes.
Add the whole bunch of mint and the sugar, pushing the leaves under the surface.
Keep over low heat 3–4 minutes without boiling — boiling scorches the mint and turns the tea bitter.
Pour out one glass and return it to the pot three times, to mix without bruising the leaves.
Pour into glasses from about 30cm up — the stream creates the foam that marks tea made properly.

recipes.title: Oranges with Cinnamon and Blossom Water
recipes.description: The dessert that closes every Moroccan meal: cold orange slices with cinnamon and orange blossom. Five minutes of work.
instructions: Peel the oranges down to the flesh with a sharp knife — all the bitter white pith must go.
Slice into rounds half a centimetre thick and lay in a single layer on a flat plate.
Sprinkle over the orange blossom water and dust evenly with icing sugar.
Scatter the cinnamon in lines rather than evenly — it looks better that way.
Chill at least an hour so the flavours soak in.
Before serving scatter over the toasted almonds, dates and torn mint leaves.

recipes.title: Zriga — Almond Milk Drink
recipes.description: A cold milk drink with ground almonds, orange blossom and cinnamon. Served very cold in tall glasses — a dairy recipe.
instructions: Blanch the almonds in boiling water for a minute and peel if needed. Grind as finely as possible in a processor.
Heat the milk with the sugar and cinnamon stick to just below boiling — do not let it boil.
Take off the heat, add the ground almonds and leave to infuse 20 minutes.
Strain through muslin or a fine sieve, pressing hard to get all the liquid out.
Stir in the orange blossom water and ground cinnamon and chill at least 3 hours.
Serve very cold in tall glasses with flaked almonds on top. A dairy recipe — not for a meat meal.

recipes.title: Fekkas — Moroccan Biscotti
recipes.description: Hard, crisp cookies with almonds, raisins and sesame, baked twice. Made for dipping in tea and they keep a month.
instructions: Beat the eggs with the sugar until pale, then add the oil and lemon zest.
Add the flour, baking powder, anise and salt and knead to a soft dough.
Fold in the almonds, raisins and sesame — gently, so the almonds stay whole.
Shape 3 long flat loaves about 7cm wide and set on a lined tray.
Bake at 180°C for about 25 minutes until lightly golden. Remove and cool 15 minutes — important, or they crumble when cut.
Slice on the diagonal 1cm thick, return to the tray and bake again at 150°C for about 20 minutes until fully dry.

recipes.title: Date and Walnut Balls
recipes.description: Dates, walnuts and orange blossom with no baking at all. A natural sweet that takes twenty minutes.

ingredients.name: desiccated coconut or sesame for rolling

instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 5 minutes until fragrant. Cool and chop roughly — keep half a cup aside.
Blitz the dates in a food processor to a sticky paste. If they are dry, soak in hot water 10 minutes and pat dry.
Add most of the walnuts, the cinnamon, orange zest, orange blossom water and oil. Pulse to an even mixture.
Fold in the reserved chopped walnuts and the sesame by hand, so some texture remains.
Roll into walnut-sized balls with slightly damp hands.
Roll in coconut or sesame and chill an hour to firm up. They keep two weeks in the fridge.
